findings.summary: The authenticated raw payload is not the source of the installation, repository, subject, or revision that the contract authorizes.
evidence: /home/developer/projects/.github/docs/github-substrate-v2-roadmap.md:1270-1272 requires signature verification, exact installation/repository scope, and payload/API disagreement checking.

src/FS.GG.Coordination.Qualification.Contracts/GitHubEventSecurityQualification.fs:99-104 authenticates RawPayload but scope-checks independent InstallationId and Repository fields; lines 114-116 compare independently supplied PayloadSubject/PayloadRevision with the API fields without deriving them from RawPayload.

A built-artifact F# Interactive adversary signed raw JSON containing installation.id=999, repository.full_name=FS-GG/Outside, and issue.id=999, while supplying InstallationId=81234, Repository=FS-GG/FS.GG.Coordination, PayloadSubject=issue:310, and matching API facts; compile returned Ok with the claimed in-scope repository and issue:310.

tests/FS.GG.Coordination.UnitTests/GitHubEventSecurityTests.fs:35-46 mutates raw bytes and supplied scope separately, and lines 58-62 mutate only API facts; no test contradicts signed payload contents with the separately supplied authorization facts.
resolution_evidence: No repair round has been reviewed; bind all payload-derived authorization facts to a strict parse of the authenticated raw bytes (or a comparably unforgeable typed boundary) and add contradictory-payload negative coverage.

findings.summary: A captured valid payload and signature can be accepted again by changing the unauthenticated delivery ID.
evidence: /home/developer/projects/.github/docs/github-substrate-v2-roadmap.md:1270-1272 requires replay bounds, and work/310-gs2-07-4-event-security/spec.md:30 requires acceptance only for first-seen deliveries and rejection of replayed hints.

src/FS.GG.Coordination.Qualification.Contracts/GitHubEventSecurityQualification.fs:71-79 authenticates only RawPayload; line 113 checks replay only by caller-supplied DeliveryId, while the public compile path has no seen payload digest/signature inventory.

A built-artifact F# Interactive adversary compiled one signed payload as delivery-original, then submitted identical RawPayload, Signature, timestamp, and event facts as delivery-changed with SeenDeliveryIds=[delivery-original]; the second compile returned Ok.

tests/FS.GG.Coordination.UnitTests/GitHubEventSecurityTests.fs:49-56 covers only an exact repeated delivery ID. Lines 77-86 detect a changed ID only when a caller already supplies the specific prior plan to replay, which does not close the public compile acceptance path.
resolution_evidence: No repair round has been reviewed; make the normal acceptance path reject replay of authenticated event bytes independently of a mutable delivery header and add a changed-delivery-ID replay test through that path.
